answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before trading, forfeited if peers prove fraud. One fake identity is cheap, but a ripple of fake accounts multiplies the locked capital, while honest agents keep their stake. Like umber dye marking counterfeit notes, a public registry flags identities whose deposits were slashed, so fresh accounts from the same operator inherit suspicion. A nebula of cheap identities collapses because every copy must pay the same bond, turning scale from an advantage into a cost.
